────────────────────────────────────────
ULID:      01KK60VVZRX87B64NJTRN0QYA1
Type:      task
Status:    pending
Priority:  2
Automation: eligible

─── Description ───
  The agent spawner (src/agents/spawner.ts) passes process.env directly to child processes. When the daemon runs inside a Claude Code session, CLAUDECODE=1 leaks into spawned agents, triggering nested-session detection and failing all dispatch invocations. Fix: strip known host-environment variables (CLAUDECODE, CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION) from inherited env before spawning. Must include unit test verifying env sanitization to prevent regression. See GitHub issue #700. Community PR #702 has the right approach but needs tests.
Spec ref:  @agent-invocation-lifecycle
Tags:      bug, agent, dispatch
Created:   2026-03-08T06:06:31.415Z

─── Spec Context ───
Agent Invocation Lifecycle
Type: feature
Implementation: implemented
Description:
  Per-invocation session creation, ACP agent spawn, prompt delivery,
  event logging, timeout handling, and structured completion tracking.
  Each dispatch creates an isolated session with its own event log and
  metadata. This is the core building block used by both the dispatch
  engine and CLI one-shot mode.
Acceptance Criteria:
  [ac-1]
    Given: An agent is dispatched for a task

    When: The invocation starts

    Then: A new session is created with trigger, agent_id, task_id, and
adapter metadata populated in session.yaml

  [ac-2]
    Given: A session is created for an agent invocation

    When: The ACP agent is spawned

    Then: KSPEC_SESSION_ID is injected into the agent environment using
the existing harness-specific injection (Claude Code, Codex, etc.)

  [ac-3]
    Given: An agent invocation is running

    When: The configured timeout_minutes is reached

    Then: The ACP client sends a cancel request, the session is closed
with status timed_out, and a timeout note is added to the task

  [ac-4]
    Given: An agent invocation completes successfully

    When: The ACP session ends with stop reason end_turn

    Then: The session is closed with status completed and an
agent.completed event is logged with structured outcome data

  [ac-5]
    Given: An agent invocation fails with a process crash or ACP error

    When: The failure is detected

    Then: The session is closed with status failed, an agent.failed
event is logged with the error details, and the task receives
a failure note

  [ac-6]
    Given: An agent invocation produces streaming output via ACP updates

    When: Session updates arrive from the ACP client

    Then: Events are logged to the session JSONL file with blob
externalization applied to oversized payloads

  [ac-7]
    Given: The prompt is built for an agent invocation

    When: The agent definition specifies skills

    Then: Skills are resolved from the skill registry and their content
is included in the prompt sent to the agent

  [ac-8]
    Given: An agent invocation completes (success or failure)

    When: Cleanup runs

    Then: The adapter env injection is restored to its previous state
and the ACP agent process is terminated if still running

  [ac-9]
    Given: An agent encounters consecutive failures on the same task

    When: The failure count reaches the agent's configured retry limit

    Then: The task is blocked with a failure note describing the
consecutive failures and the agent definition that failed

  [ac-10]
    Given: an agent definition references skills and the agent uses a specific adapter (e.g. claude-agent-acp or codex-acp)
    When: skill content is injected into the prompt via buildPromptWithSkills
    Then: cross-skill references using {skill:foo} notation are rewritten to the adapter-appropriate invocation format before injection: /foo for claude-agent-acp (Claude Code slash commands), $foo for codex-acp (Codex CLI), and {skill:foo} left as-is for unknown adapters
  [ac-11]
    Given: the ACP agent sends a request_permission or other JSON-RPC request during a tool call
    When: the invocation is running in autonomous dispatch mode
    Then: the ACP client request handler auto-approves the request by sending the appropriate response, so tool calls (Edit, Write, Bash) are never blocked waiting for human confirmation
  [ac-12]
    Given: An agent subprocess is spawned by the dispatch engine or one-shot kspec agent run
    When: The parent process environment contains variables that would interfere with agent startup (e.g. CLAUDECODE=1 causing nested-session detection)
    Then: The spawner strips known host-environment variables (CLAUDECODE, CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION) from the inherited process.env before merging adapter.env and invocation env overrides, so the agent starts cleanly without inheriting the parent's session context

{"body":"## Bug

When the kspec daemon is started from within a Claude Code environment (e.g., Claude-Terminal), the `CLAUDECODE=1` environment variable is inherited by the daemon process. When the dispatch engine spawns agent subprocesses via the ACP adapter, they also inherit this variable. Claude Code detects `CLAUDECODE=1` and refuses to start, exiting with:

```
Error: Claude Code cannot be launched inside another Claude Code session.
Nested sessions share runtime resources and will crash all active sessions.
```
